headline: Resource-efficient re-implementations and benchmarks for large-scale sequence analysis
label: Scalable Sequence Analysis Tools
summary: Native and pipeline-based tools now pair large runtime and memory gains with accuracy benchmarks on ancient, viral, and metagenomic data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is making established sequence and abundance analysis steps tractable at scale, with resource metrics reported directly. The native Python ANCOM-BC implementation in scikit-bio reports a 100-fold runtime speedup and 87% memory reduction relative to the R implementation. MAT-classifier targets memory-efficient genus-level profiling of ancient metagenomes and outperforms aMeta in simulated accuracy. ViralClust packages five clustering algorithms in a modular Nextflow pipeline to select bias-aware representative viral genomes. The metagenomic Hi-C benchmark compares seven read-alignment strategies, with BWA MEM -5SP yielding the most inter-contig pairs. The PCR bias study is adjacent, assessing how amplification bias affects alpha- and beta-diversity metrics. What is new is the pairing of resource engineering with comparative accuracy evaluation, as in the MAT-classifier simulations and the alignment benchmark.
